chunks: And the Sheikh — may Allah support him — informed me, from Abū al-Qāsim Ja'far ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn 'Īsā, from Muḥammad ibn 'Ubayd Allāh and 'Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīra — they both said:
We asked al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) about a man who sleeps on his mount.
He said: "If sleep takes away the intellect, then let him repeat the wudu."

key_terms.اَلنَّوْمُ: sleep — the act that nullifies wudu when it overcomes consciousness
key_terms.اَلْعَقْلِ: intellect/consciousness — its loss is the juristic criterion for invalidation of wudu
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ritual ablution) — must be repeated if sleep eliminates consciousness
key_terms.دَابَّتِهِ: his mount/riding animal — the circumstantial context in which the ruling was sought

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping on a mount nullify wudu according to Imam al-Riḍā (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling by Imam al-Riḍā (AS) regarding a man who falls asleep on his mount. The Imam establishes that the criterion for sleep nullifying wudu is the loss of rational consciousness — deep sleep that overwhelms the 'aql (intellect/awareness) invalidates wudu, while drowsiness that does not eliminate consciousness does not. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for enumerating the nawāqiḍ (nullifiers) of ritual purity.
